explain.say: Imagine a wall through the middle of your city, with guards, and your grandparents on the other side. For 28 years, Berlin was like that. Then in 1989, one change led to another, like falling dominoes. The board shows that chain.

explain.say: Look at the first link. In 1985 Mikhail Gorbachev became leader of the Soviet Union. He brought glasnost, which means openness, and perestroika, which means rebuilding. He also chose not to send tanks to keep Eastern Europe in line. How might people react to that?

faq.a: Mikhail Gorbachev, Soviet leader from 1985, introduced glasnost, or openness, allowing more free speech, and perestroika, or rebuilding the economy. He also stopped using force to control Eastern Europe, which let change spread.
A trade union started in 1980 at the Gdansk shipyard in Poland, led by electrician Lech Walesa. It grew into a huge movement for freedom and won partly free elections in June 1989.

faq.q: Why did Hungary open its border?
faq.a: Hungary's reforming government began taking down its border fence with Austria in May 1989. In September it let East Germans cross freely, and thousands fled to West Germany this way.
asks: How did East Germans escape in 1989?

faq.q: How did the Berlin Wall fall?
faq.a: On 9 November 1989, East German spokesman Gunter Schabowski wrongly announced that new travel rules took effect immediately. Huge crowds gathered at the checkpoints, and the guards finally opened the gates.
asks: Why did the Berlin Wall open?

faq.q: When did the Soviet Union end?
faq.a: The Soviet Union was dissolved in December 1991, and its 15 republics, including Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan and the Baltic states, became independent countries.
asks: How did the USSR break up?

facts: The Berlin Wall stood from 1961 to 1989.
The Berlin Wall was opened on 9 November 1989.

quiz.say: What does the Russian word glasnost mean?
quiz.why: Gorbachev's glasnost allowed more open discussion and free speech.

wrong.1: Glasnost was about openness, the opposite of a wall.
wrong.2: It describes a policy of openness, not a win.

quiz.say: How long did the Berlin Wall stand?
quiz.why: It was built in 1961 and opened in 1989.

wrong.1: It was built in 1961, so it stood much less than a century.
wrong.2: It stood from 1961 to 1989, far longer than two years.
